Issued at 333 AM CDT Wed Sep 9 2026

     TODAY AND THURSDAY...

Early this morning, water vapor satellite imagery and upper air 
analysis shows a vort max rounding the southern end of broad trough 
over southern Canada with a stream of moisture extending from the 
eastern Pacific to the Great Lakes. At the surface, a stalled cold 
front is draped across Kansas from the northern KC metro to Liberal. 
Additionally, broad mid-level WAA extends from the Upper Midwest to 
eastern Colorado supporting the continuation of isolated to widely 
scattered showers and storms across northern and western portions of 
Kansas despite ample and widespread convective inhibition. 
Throughout the day, the aforementioned cold front and mid-level 
baroclinic zone will sag southward. A few elevated showers and 
storms are possible this morning into early afternoon across central 
Kansas. Later in the afternoon, sufficient destabilization is likely 
to occur across south-central and southeast Kansas thanks to 
moisture pooling along the frontal boundary and ample diurnal 
heating. Model soundings from almost the entire 00Z CAM suite show a 
classic inverted-v profile along the frontal boundary. With a few 
thunderstorms expected to develop along the cold front and shear 
being fairly meager (under 15-20 knots of 0-6 km shear likely), 
microbursts producing 55-65 mph wind gusts are possible. Coverage of 
thunderstorms this afternoon remains somewhat in question which is 
why medium PoPs (30-50%) were held between 18-00Z today across 
southern and southeast Kansas. In addition to storm chances, the 
heat and humidity south of the approaching cold front will support 
another afternoon with heat indices between 105 and 109 across south-
central and southeast Kansas.

The loss of diurnal heating after 00Z will support a brief lull in 
shower and thunderstorm activity across the southern half of Kansas 
late this evening into early tonight. However, with the mid-level 
baroclinic zone still forecast to be over southern Kansas along with 
the LLJ slightly ramping up after sunset, scattered to potentially 
numerous showers and thunderstorms are anticipated to develop south 
of the I-70 corridor after 03Z. The 00Z CAMs showed a decent uptick 
in convection overnight tonight through much of Thursday, and this 
makes sense given ample mid-level WAA and an approaching shortwave 
trough trekking eastward out over the central and northern plains. 
It's possible a few of these storms could be strong with heavy 
rainfall and frequent lightning, but the overall damaging wind 
threat will be lower than this afternoon. The primary concern for 
activity overnight through Thursday morning will be the potential 
for localized flooding given very high PWATs (over 2 inches) and 
possible training thunderstorms along the frontal boundary/mid-level 
baroclinic zone. However, some of these concerns will be mitigated 
by the fact that it has been incredibly dry over the past 2 months 
or so. Still, some low-lying and flood prone areas could see some 
flooding if thunderstorms train over the same area for several 
hours. As the baroclinic zone continues drifting southward on 
Thursday, and broad subsidence overspreads the region, rain chances 
will gradually end from north to south. Given ample cloud cover 
throughout the day, it's likely much of the region will see the 
coolest afternoon highs (mid 80s) in almost 50 days!

     FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY...

The forecast becomes a bit more uncertain by the end of the work 
week through the beginning of next week. Global mid-range guidance 
is signaling zonal upper flow increasing across the central plains 
by Friday with potentially a series of embedded shortwave troughs 
traversing eastward over the region Friday through the beginning of 
next week. Some of the aforementioned mid range guidance is hinting 
at several rounds of showers and storms Friday night through Sunday 
morning across eastern Kansas. However, there's still enough spread 
in the guidance for only medium (30-60%) chances for showers and 
storms in this period. Active weather is possible for the beginning 
of next week as well. However, the spread in long range global 
models is leading to low confidence in the forecast this far out. 
Despite PoPs in the forecast for Sunday night through Tuesday night, 
this may be subject to change in future forecasts.
